exposure: Preoperative cervical length (categorized as 0-0.4 cm, 0.5-1.4 cm, 1.5-2.4 cm, and >= 2.5 cm)
Diagnostic types of cervical insufficiency (obstetric history-based, ultrasound-based, physical examination-based)
cohort: The study included 168 patients diagnosed with various types of cervical insufficiency who underwent cervical cerclage.
finding: Longer preoperative cervical length was significantly associated with better outcomes in terms of gestational prolongation and newborn survival after cervical cerclage.
